gate_reasoning: Stage 4 contains 63 scored claims with 69.8% Low confidence — materially higher than the threshold that warrants a targeted deep-research pass rather than a full re-run. The 7 High-confidence claims (11.1%) are well-evidenced anchor points: e2open SEC filing, DHL audited annual report, DSV investor relations regulatory disclosure, McKinsey logistics handover report, TT Club/BSI 2025 Cargo Theft Report (cited three times), and IUMI/TAPA EMEA crime statistics. The structural quality of the draft is good — the 8-9 ASSUMED tags are properly labeled, the market-size table carries explicit confidence ratings, and the data-gap declaration on SEA-specific control tower penetration is appropriately honest. The three most consequential weak-claim clusters are: (1) the Gartner/MIT CTL disruption statistics (34 system updates, 25 emails) accessible only through FourKites' vendor blog — these anchor PP4.2 severity and need primary corroboration; (2) the Mordor-only SEA trucking fragmentation figures (84% Vietnam owner-operators, ASEAN median fleet size) that underpin the SEA-specific WH2 case across PP4.1 and PP4.5 — these need government statistics or ADB/World Bank cross-validation; and (3) the enterprise control-tower pricing figure ($200K-$500K+) from a single blog source with no methodology. The draft should ship to the next stage with these three deep-research priorities flagged, but does not require a full re-run given the strength of the structural framing and the quality of the High-tier evidence anchors.
